results.title: 🇲🇱 Mali is bleeding. At least 48 civilians from the Idaksahak community were killed when ISIS fighters attacked Tagadayat village in the Mén
results.description:
🇲🇱 Mali is bleeding. 

At least 48 civilians from the Idaksahak community were killed when ISIS fighters attacked Tagadayat village in the Ménaka region on October 19.

The attackers accused residents of sharing information about their positions with the Malian army ahead of a drone strike. Several people were wounded, and families fled toward Ménaka.

Civilians continue to pay the price of the Sahel's escalating security crisis.

results.title: Africa Corps under pressure: the 🌴Sahel, April–October 2026 Russia promised security to the Sahel’s military regimes.
results.description:
Africa Corps under pressure: the 🌴Sahel, April–October 2026

Russia promised security to the Sahel’s military regimes. The facts tell a different story.

🇲🇱 Mali: On 25 April, coordinated 🥷JNIM and FLA attacks struck several locations, including Bamako and Kati. Defence Minister Sadio Camara was killed and Kidal fell to the FLA. On 10 September, JNIM overran Dioura, reportedly killing over 100 Malian soldiers and five Africa Corps personnel. Russian-backed forces returned to Kidal in October after the FLA withdrew—but holding it remains the real test.

🇧🇫 Burkina Faso: JNIM continues to inflict heavy losses. At least 34 civilians were reportedly executed in Titao in February; around 90 soldiers were reportedly killed in a September ambush at Koubel-Alpha.

🇳🇪 Niger: More than 50 security personnel were reportedly killed in two September attacks. Even Niamey’s military infrastructure has been targeted. Africa Corps has not stopped the insurgency.

The verdict: Russia’s presence has not delivered security. The 🇺🇸US State Department advises Americans NOT TO TRAVEL to all three AES countries.

#AES #Sahel #Mali #BurkinaFaso #Niger #JNIM

results.title: #BreakingNews: 48 civilians reportedly killed in Mali attack.
results.description:
#BreakingNews: 48 civilians reportedly killed in Mali attack.

An attack attributed to Islamic State-linked militants reportedly killed 48 civilians in Mali’s eastern Ménaka region, according to a Tuareg leader cited by the Associated Press.

Children and elderly people were among the victims.

The attack highlights the continuing security challenges facing communities across the Sahel.
